newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities steady to easier.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt volatilities steady to easier.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. fixed income options were steady to easier in slow midsession trading as underlying markets drifted narrowly at slightly weaker levels, dealers said.
"Obviously it was a little higher before all the numbers came out," said a Treasury bond trader for a brokerage at the Chicago Board of Trade. "It's come off a little bit now."
Implied volatility for April T-bond futures options was off 0.1 point at midsession at around 9.25 percent, while June volatility was virtually unchanged at 9.5 percent.

Although the underlying market has held to a narrow range so far this week, traders noted that market makers were wary of pushing option prices lower as implied volatilities were already at historically low levels.

"Relative to what vols have been, that's pretty darn low," the brokerage trader said of today's volatility levels. He noted that front-month CBOT futures options have tended to trade mostly between 9.5 and 10.5 percent in recent years.
Traders added that concerns about a downward correction in bond prices after a month-long rally also underpinned volatilities.
They said the bond market's lackluster performance today despite news of a soft January consumer price index (CPI) could be signalling that the market was running out of steam.
Both the overall CPI and the core rate, excluding food and energy, rose 0.1 percent in January, slightly below average Wall Street forecasts, but bond prices barely reacted.

March 113 puts, which expire on Friday, were traded in large lots several times, most likely on speculation of an imminent downturn, traders said. At least three firms were seen buying about 2,000 each of the contract.

With premium at around 1/4 point against March futures at around 113-20/32 and very high gamma, or premium acceleration, due to the short life to maturity, one trader said the contract was like a "cheap lottery ticket".

Still, even though the strike price was less than a point away from the futures price, the delta of the contract was not very high and was shrinking quickly because of the short life, he added. Thus the options would need a quick, sharp drop in futures to be profitable. Delta is the rate at which premium moves per change in the underlying bond price.
At the shorter end of the market, Eurodollar volatilities were mostly steady, slightly softer at the front end.
Implied volatility for June futures options was off a few tenths at 8.0 percent, while September was virtually unchanged at 12.2 percent.
